MFSTNet · lane placement · 19 Aug 2026

Place The Lanes

The heat shows where vehicles actually were, over 30 sampled frames. Four crosses are already placed on every camera — your job is to move the ones sitting in the wrong place, not to start from nothing. Keep it at four everywhere.

Why by hand

  1. Measured: automatic centres move 0.164 of the frame width — about 315 px — when the detector changes. A lane that moves when the tooling changes is not a property of the road.
  2. Why four, and why the same four everywhere. The congestion head is built once with one output per lane, so a corpus cannot mix a two-lane camera with a four-lane one. Four is the count that earns its place: at two centres, South Extension left 35.1% of vehicles outside every lane and video1 44.4%, both failing the corpus gate. At four every camera passes, the worst being 10.5%.
  3. The seeded crosses are a clustering, not a judgement. They sit at the centre of mass of the detections, which lands them on the busiest part of a lane — sometimes a junction's middle where two approaches merge. Move a cross onto the approach you mean; that is the part a clustering cannot do.
  4. Nothing here is expensive any more. Counts are re-derived from stored detections in under a second, so a placement can be tried, measured against its unassigned rate, and changed. It does not have to be right first time.
  5. The heat map is the aid, not the authority: it shows where the detector saw traffic, and on dense Indian scenes the detector misses a lot. Place the cross where the approach is, not where the heat is.
  6. Order does not matter — lanes are renamed left-to-right on import.
  7. When you are done, Copy JSON puts the whole thing on the clipboard — paste it back into the chat. The box below always holds the current state, so selecting it by hand works too.
